topic: OpenBot Review 2026: AI Coworkers That Each Get a Computer of Their Own

key_points: OpenBot is CopilotKit's open-source (MIT) platform where each AI coworker gets its own computer: a real browser with its own logins, its own files, and only the tools you grant.
Core principle: 'Every action decided before it happens and recorded after.' A gateway resolves the target, evaluates CEL policy, writes an audit row, then acts or refuses while naming the rule.
Framework-agnostic — brings any AG-UI agent (LangGraph, CrewAI, Mastra, Pydantic AI, Google ADK) as a coworker with a channel of its own.
Created 17 Aug 2026; ~5.2k stars, 663 forks, v0.0.13 latest release, 406 commits, 29 contributors. Alpha, under active development.
Runs on Docker Compose + your own PostgreSQL. No model ships in the box; an admin supplies the credential, encrypted at rest and never logged.
Three example coworkers ship as configuration: General Assistant, Knowledge, Risk Analyst.
Giving an agent a browser with real logins is the point where what it is allowed to do becomes an operational question, not just a design one.
The decide-then-record split is the differentiator: deciding before is a policy check; recording after is an audit trail. Most tools today only do the recording.
Warns the same gap shown in OpenAI's postmortem of its agents reaching Hugging Face production systems — the intrusion was recorded, not prevented.
Practical advice: start with an agent with read-only access to something unimportant and read tool grants line by line before widening.
Flags OPENBOT_SINGLE_USER=true (ships in .env.example) as a security gap — it admits every request as one admin; turn it off before exposing the deployment.
Frames OpenBot around the agentic trust boundary: enterprises need audited, isolated execution before deploying autonomous agents.

Key features: dedicated computer per coworker (isolated Docker container, optional gVisor runsc kernel sandboxing), fail-closed CEL policy gateway, take-the-wheel human intervention, universal AG-UI compatibility, generative UI components.
Human handover: on 2FA/CAPTCHA/high-risk events the agent pauses and a human takes over the browser canvas directly, then hands control back seamlessly.
Generative UI: coworkers render rich interactive React components (dashboards, forms) directly into channels, not just markdown.
Single-image quickstart: docker run with EMBEDDED_POSTGRES=on.
Architecture: one gateway server plus one container per bot; each bot has its own Chromium, workspace volume and persistent browser profile.
The gateway on port 3001 is the only path to a bot's computer; it resolves the target, evaluates CEL rules, writes an audit row, then calls the container. The computer does not decide policy.
Policy is deny-by-default with deny rules evaluated before allow rules; a missing policy permits nothing, and a broken rule fails toward blocking.
Published resource figures (one Bot, arm64, Aug 2026): measured 0.55 GB RAM / 5.3 GB disk / 0.06 vCPU; documented minimum 2 GB / 8 GB / 1 vCPU; recommended 4 GB / 10 GB / 2 vCPU.
Disk is the cost you forget: Chromium launches with --disable-dev-shm-usage writing to /tmp, and the image ships Playwright's Firefox and WebKit binaries.
OPENBOT_SINGLE_USER is a laptop setting — on a VPS the first person to reach the port owns the deployment, stored credentials and signed-in browser.
OpenBot hit 3,364 stars by 29 Aug 2026 (created 17 Aug), and 1,089 stars in its first three days.

Every action against a computer, file, MCP server or UI component routes through a single gateway that resolves, decides against policy, writes an audit row, then acts or refuses while naming the rule.
Each bot gets its own container with its own Chromium, logins and workspace.
Agents arrive over AG-UI so LangGraph, Mastra, CrewAI, Pydantic AI and Google ADK agents connect identically without a framework binding.
MIT-licensed alpha; runs on Docker Compose against your own PostgreSQL; no model ships in the box; admin credentials encrypted at rest.

stats.fact: OpenBot was created on 17 August 2026 and by late September 2026 had ~5,200 GitHub stars, 663 forks, 21 watchers and 29 contributors.
OpenBot reached 3,364 stars by 29 Aug 2026 and 1,089 stars in its first three days.
As of 31 Aug 2026, OpenBot had 3,598 stars and 449 forks under an MIT license.
Latest tagged release v0.0.13 (18 Sep 2026); 406 commits total; code is 84.6% TypeScript and 12.3% Rust.
Published resource usage for one Bot (arm64, Aug 2026): 0.55 GB RAM peak, 5.3 GB disk, 0.06 vCPU; documented minimum 2 GB RAM / 8 GB disk / 1 vCPU; recommended 4 GB RAM / 10 GB disk / 2 vCPU.
OpenBot is MIT-licensed alpha software under active development that expects rough edges.
For comparison, OpenAI's computer-use agent (Operator) scored 38.1% on OSWorld and 58.1% on WebArena, and costs $200/mo via ChatGPT Pro.

angles: Decide-then-record governance is the real differentiator — a fail-closed, deny-by-default CEL policy gateway checks EVERY action before it runs and writes an audit row after; most competing tools only log afterward.

Per-coworker isolated computer: each bot gets its own Chromium, its own logins, its own workspace and only the tools you grant — a browser profile is an identity and shared sessions are the security failure mode.
Framework-agnostic via AG-UI: bring any agent (LangGraph, CrewAI, Mastra, Pydantic AI, Google ADK) and it becomes a coworker — no framework binding.
Self-hosted and BYO-model: runs on Docker Compose + your own PostgreSQL, no model ships in the box, admin supplies credentials encrypted at rest — data and credentials never leave your network.
Human take-the-wheel handovers: agent pauses on 2FA/CAPTCHA/high-risk steps and a human takes over the live browser canvas, then hands control back.

Positioning vs cloud giants: unlike OpenAI Operator (browser-only, $200/mo, confirmation-obsessed) and Claude computer use (API-driven), OpenBot is open-source, self-hostable and per-bot isolated — the governance-first alternative.
Caution angle: OPENBOT_SINGLE_USER=true ships by default and admits every request as one admin; alpha software + real credentials + a real browser is the combination to be slow about.
